definitions.SESSION_TIME: timestamp of the session/message the memory item was formed from
definitions.EVENT_TIME: the time of the event described in the fact
definitions.RESOLVED_EVENT_TIME: an event time unambiguously derivable from the fact's own text plus a reference date
definitions.TEMPORAL_ALIGNMENT.ALIGNED: session time is a good proxy for event time on this reasoning task
definitions.TEMPORAL_ALIGNMENT.DIVERGENT: session time and event time differ in a way that could change the answer
definitions.TEMPORAL_ALIGNMENT.AMBIGUOUS: cannot be safely determined from available evidence
definitions.TEMPORAL_ALIGNMENT.NON_TEMPORAL: time is not material to the question

[2023-11-30] Has 17 new postcards since starting collecting again

stage2_units.question: How many engineers do I lead when I just started my new role as Senior Software Engineer? How many engineers do I lead now?
relevant_fact_text: [2023-05-11] New role as Senior Software Engineer
stage2_units.event_time_status: EXPLICIT (session-anchor dates only; no additional in-text date on either fact)
stage2_units.notes: Only ONE team-size fact ('4 engineers') is retrievable anywhere in the delivered context, anchored five months after the new-role fact. BASE silently treated '4' as the starting count (matching only half of gold, apparently enough for the binary judge). +TIME correctly notices the anchor gap and refuses to assume '4' is the STARTING count, producing an honest, well-founded hedge that the binary judge then scores wrong because it no longer flatly asserts a number. This is a genuine, positive engagement with the session-time signal that the judge protocol penalizes, not a reasoning failure.
stage2_units.wrong_answer_traceability: NOT_APPLICABLE -- the +TIME answer contains no fabricated or wrong factual content; the change is an added hedge/omission, not a false claim traceable to a sibling item
stage2_units.effect: HURT (via judge-penalized epistemic caution, not via a temporal-reasoning error)

stage2_units.question: Where do I currently keep my old sneakers?
relevant_fact_text: [2023-05-25] Has old sneakers stored under bed that smell
[2023-05-29] Planning to store old sneakers in a shoe rack
stage2_units.notes: Gold ('shoe rack in closet') matches the LATER-dated fact, but that fact is phrased as a PLAN ('planning to store'), not a confirmed completed action; the EARLIER-dated fact states the CURRENT stored location in the present tense ('has... stored under bed'). Both arms default to the earlier, confirmed-state fact over the later, merely-intended one -- a defensible reading that dates alone do not resolve, since the real ambiguity is plan-vs-executed, not which fact is more recent. Documented at selection time as a weak-fit TEMPORAL_POSITIVE case (current-state lookup); this confirms that characterization.
stage2_units.wrong_answer_traceability: TRACEABLE (both arms' 'under the bed' answer is a genuine stored fact, not confabulated) but reflects a plan-vs-executed reasoning gap, not entity confusion
stage2_units.effect: NEUTRAL (wrong in both arms, unaffected by anchoring)

stage2_units.question: How many days had passed between the Sunday mass at St. Mary's Church and the Ash Wednesday service at the cathedral?

[2023-02-20] Attended Sunday mass at St. Mary's Church on January 2nd
stage2_units.event_time_status: EXPLICIT (each fact states its own event date directly in-text: 'on February 1st', 'on January 2nd')
stage2_units.temporal_alignment: DIVERGENT (session anchor 2023-02-20 differs from both in-text event dates) but NOT HARMFUL here
stage2_units.notes: Both needed event dates are explicit in the fact text itself; the reader's +TIME answer quotes exactly those in-text dates ('January 2nd', 'February 1st'), not the shared session anchor, and computes 30 days, matching gold. BASE, given the identical fact text without any rendered anchor, answered 'cannot be determined' despite the dates being present in the text all along -- suggesting the uniform per-item date tag increased the reader's propensity to actively parse and compare in-text dates across a long list, rather than supplying information that was otherwise missing. INFERENCE, not directly provable from a single transcript pair.

stage2_units.question: How many doctor's appointments did I go to in March?
session_timestamps_delivered: 2023-03-27 (shared session anchor for both target facts and several unrelated March-tagged facts)
relevant_fact_text: [2023-03-27] Diagnosed with bronchitis by Dr. Smith on March 3rd
[2023-03-27] Had a follow-up appointment with orthopedic surgeon Dr. Thompson on March 20th, knee is healing well
stage2_units.event_time_status: EXPLICIT (each fact states its own event date in-text: 'March 3rd', 'March 20th')
stage2_units.temporal_alignment: DIVERGENT and HARMFUL: the shared session anchor (March 27, itself in March) sits alongside several other same-session facts unrelated to doctor visits, all bearing the identical tag
stage2_units.notes: This is the clearest genuine negative-transfer case in the sample. Content is unchanged between arms; only the per-item date tag was added. BASE correctly lists both March visits from their in-text dates. +TIME drops the bronchitis visit and undercounts to 1. Both target facts DO carry explicit in-text dates (ruling out a pure 'anchor replaces missing date' story, cf. 08f4fc43 where anchoring helped despite an identical structural setup). The differentiating factor appears to be TASK TYPE: 08f4fc43/0bc8ad92 are two-item duration lookups; 00ca467f is a filter-and-count task across many same-session items sharing one identical tag, several of which are medical-adjacent but not appointments (Dr. Patel gastroenterology consideration, Dr. Smith/Johnson hand-numbness planning). INFERENCE, not fully provable from one transcript pair: the uniform, repeated session tag may compete with in-text dates specifically under a counting/filtering task, in a way it does not under a two-item lookup task.
stage2_units.timestamp_used_by_reader: YES (but leading to a worse outcome)

h5_primary_case_E1_gpt4_f420262c.question: What is the order of airlines I flew with from earliest to latest before today?
h5_primary_case_E1_gpt4_f420262c.wrong_answer_full: 1. American Airlines 2. United Airlines 3. JetBlue 4. Spirit Airlines
h5_primary_case_E1_gpt4_f420262c.search_scope: frozen mem0_3000 delivered context only (208 items), data/lab/arena/mem0-breadth-arms.json
relevant_correct_evidence_items: 0: Had a terrible in-flight entertainment system on a flight from New York to Los Angeles on February 10th
2: Had a terrible experience with American Airlines' entertainment system...
3: Took a round-trip flight from Boston to Atlanta today (the Delta flight, airline name not stated in this item)
7: Had a 1-hour delay on a United Airlines flight from Boston to Chicago...
9: Just got back from a red-eye flight on JetBlue from San Francisco to Boston...
13: Planning a trip to Miami later this year and wants to redeem Delta SkyMiles for a free trip (the multi-hop link to 'Delta' the reader needed to make)
sibling_items_found: 5: Curious about Spirit Airlines' baggage policies (rank 5, immediately adjacent to the relevant flight cluster at ranks 0,2,3,7,9)
12: Planning a spring break trip to Fort Lauderdale in March and flying Spirit Airlines (a genuine but FUTURE, not-yet-taken Spirit Airlines trip)
h5_primary_case_E1_gpt4_f420262c.reasoning: Spirit Airlines is a real, present, semantically-adjacent (same domain: airline preferences and travel plans) item at close rank proximity to the four genuinely relevant flight facts. The correct 4th airline (Delta) requires a multi-hop link between two separate items (the unnamed Boston-Atlanta flight and a separate Delta SkyMiles mention) that the reader apparently did not make; Spirit Airlines, by contrast, is directly named and sits right next to the relevant cluster, making it the path of least resistance for a 4th list entry. This is a clean, concrete instance of the harmful-sibling pattern: correct evidence present, a plausible wrong-sibling entity also present nearby, reader selects the wrong variant instead of doing the harder multi-hop resolution for the correct one.

distraction_check_stage2_repair_and_regr.method: for each of the 5 Stage 2 repair/regression units, checked whether the specific wrong (or previously-wrong, now-correct) content is traceable to a different, semantically-similar item in the same delivered context
distraction_check_stage2_repair_and_regr.result_summary: 0 of 5 Stage 2 cases show H5-style entity-level sibling distraction. 031748ae and 0977f2af's changes are hedges/omissions with no fabricated content to trace. 00ca467f's regression is a same-entity date-signal conflict (SESSION_TIME vs EVENT_TIME), mechanistically distinct from H5. 08f4fc43 and 0bc8ad92 are repairs (nothing wrong to trace); 0bc8ad92 additionally shows a near-miss distractor (a different museum visit, 'with dad') that the reader correctly avoided, recorded as a useful negative control for H5.

temporal_alignment_table.note: DIVERGENT contains both of Stage 2's real repairs (08f4fc43) counted alongside its one clean negative-transfer regression (00ca467f) and one judge-penalized-hedge regression (031748ae) -- divergence alone does not predict direction; whether the fact text carries an EXPLICIT in-text date the reader can fall back on, and whether the task is a two-item lookup vs a many-item filter/count, appear to matter more than alignment status alone.
